To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) visuo-manual interaction tasks are characterized by an intermittent motor control mechanism, (ii) the presence of a deviating force-field does not change the control patterns of the visuo-manual task, and (iii) the coordination of the two tasks is achieved by a mixture of stiffness and force control.

the coordination of the two tasks is achieved by a force/stiffness combination that depends on the implicit accuracy of visuo-manual control, and that the overall control pattern is not affected by the presence of the force field.

the visuomotor coordination in the hybrid tracking task is achieved by a mixture of force and stiffness components, and that the force component is dominant in the case of high tracking accuracy, whereas the stiffness component prevails when tracking accuracy is low.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the coordination of two sub-tasks in a hybrid task.
the study of the coordination of visuomanual tracking and force compensation, in the presence of a deviating force field.
the analysis of the coordination mechanisms underlying visuo-manual interaction with a dynamic environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the visuo-manual task is characterized by an intermittence control mechanism that can be modified by an additional task (force compensation) but is not influenced by it.

visuo-maninal tracking is a hybrid task in the sense that it is a combination of two different tasks, one for tracking and one for force compensation; the control strategies for the two sub-task are different but they are integrated by a common strategy based on a combination of stiffness and direct force components.
the control of the interaction-forces is based on the combination of arm stiffness and direct force control and is achieved by an intermittent control strategy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in a complex visuo-manual task, a large deviating field can be easily learnt and controlled by the subject, with a negligible effect on the visuo-manual control.

, in the presence of a deviating force field in a hybrid tracking task, the control of the force field is achieved by a direct force control component and by an implicit stiffness component, while the visuo-manual control is achieved by an intermittent control strategy, with a high level of coordination between the two sub-task controls.

the visuo-manual control of the tracking error is achieved by a hybrid control mechanism that combines stiffness and force control, while the compensation of the deviating field is performed by the same mechanism, which is a function, however, of the tracking accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the visuomotor control system can be considered as a whole, in that the control of movement and the control of forces are not independent, but rather are coupled in order to achieve an optimal performance.
the control of the two subtasks can be achieved with a simple and effective strategy that does not require the subject to learn a complex coordination of the two components.
the intermittent control mechanism is robust against large perturbations, provided that the subject is able to learn the task and the perturbation.
